Re: Mutual Confidentiality Agreement

Dear Ms. Fjeldstad:

This letter sets out the terms on which Calloway Biosciences, Inc. ("Calloway") and Vantablack Therapeutics AS ("Vantablack") will exchange confidential information in connection with a possible collaboration relating to allosteric modulators of the GPR52 receptor (the "Purpose"). Each of us may act as a discloser and as a recipient, and the obligations below apply to each of us in that capacity.

1. Confidential Information. "Confidential Information" means any information a party or its Representatives discloses to the other, in any form, that is marked confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances of disclosure. It includes preclinical and clinical data, assay protocols, compound structures, manufacturing processes, regulatory correspondence, business plans, and the fact and content of our discussions. "Representatives" means a party's directors, officers, employees, and professional advisers who need to know the information for the Purpose.

2. Exclusions. Confidential Information does not include information that (a) is or becomes public through no act or omission of the receiving party, (b) the receiving party can show by contemporaneous written records was in its possession without an obligation of confidence before disclosure, (c) is received from a third party free of any obligation of confidence, or (d) the receiving party can show by contemporaneous written records was independently developed without use of or reference to the disclosing party's Confidential Information.

3. Use and Disclosure. The receiving party will use Confidential Information solely for the Purpose, will not disclose it to anyone other than its Representatives, and will protect it with at least the care it uses for its own confidential information of like importance and in no event less than reasonable care. The receiving party is responsible for any breach of this letter by its Representatives.

4. Compelled Disclosure. If the receiving party is required by law, regulation, or an order of a court or regulator to disclose Confidential Information, it may do so, provided that it gives the disclosing party prompt written notice (unless legally prohibited) so the disclosing party may seek a protective order, discloses only the portion legally required, and uses reasonable efforts to obtain confidential treatment for what is disclosed.

5. No Licence; No Representation. Nothing in this letter grants either party any licence or other right under any patent, know-how, trademark, or other intellectual property of the other, whether by implication, estoppel, or otherwise. Neither party makes any representation or warranty as to the accuracy or completeness of its Confidential Information, and neither party will have any liability arising from the other's reliance on it.

6. Return or Destruction. On the disclosing party's written request, the receiving party will promptly return or destroy all Confidential Information in its possession and certify the destruction in writing, except that (a) it may retain one archival copy in its legal files solely to establish its obligations under this letter, and (b) it need not delete copies made by routine automated backup, which remain subject to this letter for as long as they are retained.

7. Term. This letter applies to disclosures made during the two (2) years after the date above. The obligations in Sections 3, 4, and 6 continue for five (5) years after each disclosure, except that trade secrets remain protected for as long as they qualify as trade secrets under applicable law.

8. Remedies. Each party acknowledges that a breach of this letter may cause irreparable harm for which money damages would be inadequate, and that the disclosing party is entitled to seek injunctive relief in addition to any other remedy, without the necessity of posting a bond.

9. No Obligation to Proceed. Neither of us is obliged to enter into any further agreement or transaction. This letter creates no exclusivity, no joint venture, and no obligation to negotiate.

10. Governing Law and Disputes. This letter is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules. Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts sitting in Wilmington, Delaware, and waives any objection based on forum non conveniens.

11. General. This letter is the entire agreement between us on its subject matter and supersedes any prior understanding on it. It may be amended only by a writing signed by both of us. Neither party may assign it without the other's prior written consent, except to a successor to all or substantially all of its business. It may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature.

If the foregoing reflects your understanding, please sign and return the enclosed copy.

Very truly yours,

CALLOWAY BIOSCIENCES, INC.

By: /s/ Desmond Achterberg
Desmond Achterberg
Chief Executive Officer
